_note: REAL row from production.supply_analytics.sxp_activity_criteria, exported 2026-04-18 – 2026-10-14. Scalar fields are verbatim. `supplier_name` came with the export this time. The export also carried a `supplier_email` (a personal gmail address); it is DROPPED here — this repo publishes to a public GitHub Pages site and the fixture JSON is readable in page source.
_scenario: Fails Trust & Safety on BOTH supplier-level rate rules at once — rule B (investigated case rate) and rule C (T&S tag rate) — with no severe case. The real counterpart to the synthetic `ts-tag-rate` fixture, and the first real row to fail rule B. Everything else passes: entry, rating 4.88 against 4.6, quality 0.98% against 2%. Verified against the deck: case rate 0.000493 > 0.0003 with 5.0 weighted cases; tag rate 0.778% > 0.5% with 76 tagged bookings. Both are judged on the supplier's pooled bookings, so every BFT GROUP activity is excluded, not just this one.
_note_precedence: Both rate rules fail, so the row shows the TAG-RATE copy — precedence is severe > tag rate > case rate, see criteria-model.js. No tag breakdown accompanies it because this tour has no booking-level rows at all; see _note_data_gap.
_note_next_award_date: NOT from the export. Set to the close of the intended assessment period (2027-01-01), matching every other fixture so the banner reads the same across the switcher.
_note_window: window_start/window_end are the INTENDED assessment period (Jul 1, 2026 – Jan 1, 2027), not this row's own export window (2026-04-18 – 2026-10-14). The metrics were measured over the export window, so the period label and the numbers come from different ranges — the same deliberate mismatch the other real fixtures carry.
_note_data_gap: No booking-level defect records found for this tour_id in sxp_booking_defect (0 rows total, not just within the 6-month window), despite nonzero aggregates here: quality_defect_bookings = 11, pickup_defect_bookings = 1, ts_tag_bookings = 2, supplier_ts_tag_bookings = 76. Same reconciliation gap documented in CLAUDE.md.
_note_has_badge_min: The export says has_badge_min = true while meets_ts = false. Under the old `!has_badge && has_badge_min` read that would have rendered this Trust & Safety failure as 'blocked by city bar'. criteria-model.js recomputes the outcome and ANDs meets_ts, so it correctly shows as a T&S failure — and destination_step is 0, so there is no city bar here at all. Note meets_excellence is also false in the export even though crit_rating, crit_defect_rate and crit_pickup_rate are all true: the row never reached Gate 4 because it failed T&S, so excellence was never assessed.
_note_details: INVENTED trends, not from the export — same generator and caveats as the other real fixtures. Anchored to rating_in_window (4.8783, mean of the series 4.8800) and quality_defect_rate (0.9804%, mean 0.9804%), both staying on the passing side of their bars. No pickup trend: has_pickup is false, so that row is not rendered. No disruption lists: this tour has zero rows in sxp_booking_defect.
